seo.meta_title: Is O'Charley's Closed? What Happened to the Chain in 2026
seo.meta_description: O'Charley's abruptly closed all of its company-owned restaurants on September 9, 2026, after 55 years. What happened, who owned it and what's left.

question: Is O'Charley's Closed?
quick_answer: Yes. O'Charley's abruptly closed all of its company-owned restaurants on September 9, 2026, ending a 55-year run. The Nashville-based chain had about 52 locations in 13 states at the start of 2026, down from nearly 250 at its peak. A few franchised locations in Ohio stayed open briefly after the corporate closures, but the brand is all but defunct. Its website and social media accounts were taken down.
key_facts: About 52 locations in 13 states at the start of 2026

body.heading: What happened
body.text: On September 8 and 9, 2026, O'Charley's told employees that its company-owned restaurants would close, many of them at 8 p.m. on Wednesday, September 9. Workers and customers got almost no warning. By that night, O'Charley's website showed a 'site not found' message and its Facebook and Instagram pages had been removed. The company did not make a public statement.

body.heading: Why O'Charley's closed
body.text: O'Charley's had been shrinking for years. It closed 51 restaurants in 2023 and four more in the first half of 2026 while its owner, Cannae Holdings, tried to turn sales around with menu changes and better service. That plan didn't work: Cannae's restaurant group, which includes O'Charley's, reported an operating loss of $81.9 million from July 2025 to June 2026, and O'Charley's sales fell by double digits. The closures came during a broader review of Cannae's restaurant holdings.

body.heading: Are any O'Charley's still open?
body.text: At the time of the shutdown, a franchise company in Ohio ran three O'Charley's restaurants that were not part of the corporate closures. Reports said at least one would stay open only until late September or early October 2026. Restaurant Business described the brand as all but defunct. If you're near one of the former franchised locations, call ahead before visiting.

body.heading: O'Charley's history
body.text: Charles 'Sonny' Watkins opened the first O'Charley's in 1971 near Vanderbilt University in Nashville. He sold the business in 1984 to David Wachtel, a former Shoney's executive, who grew it into a regional chain. At its peak in the 2000s, O'Charley's had nearly 250 restaurants. It was later bought by Fidelity National Financial's restaurant group and came under Cannae Holdings in 2018. It was known for its free hot yeast rolls, Famous Chicken Tenders and Famous Pies.

body.heading: Where to go instead
body.text: Fans looking for similar Southern comfort food at a sit-down chain often turn to Cheddar's Scratch Kitchen, Cracker Barrel or Texas Roadhouse. Our O'Charley's menu page still shows the last known menu prices before the closure, for reference.

faqs.q: Is O'Charley's going out of business?
faqs.a: Yes. It closed all of its company-owned restaurants on September 9, 2026. Only a few franchised locations stayed open briefly afterward.
Years of falling sales and traffic. Its owner's restaurant group lost $81.9 million in the year to June 2026, and O'Charley's sales fell by double digits.
About 52 in 13 states at the start of 2026, down from nearly 250 at its peak.
